Mango fertilizer schedule by tree age

Gujarat Bio Organics team · Checked against NHB, TNAU, KAU and JAU · Updated 26 November 2026

Short answer

A young mango tree needs about 100 g nitrogen and 100 g potash for every year of its age, with phosphorus rising from 50 g to 500 g, plus farmyard manure. Give half at the start of the monsoon and half at its end. From about year 10 the National Horticulture Board dose is 1 kg N, 500 g P and 1 kg K with 50 kg manure per tree every year. TNAU and KAU give different figures; the calculator below works out any of them for your orchard.

How much fertilizer a mango tree needs, by age

The three recommendations below are per tree per year. N is nitrogen, P is phosphorus and K is potash, in grams; manure (FYM, well-rotted farmyard manure) is in kg. We read P and K as P₂O₅ and K₂O, as in Indian packages of practices.

Tree age (years)NHB N : P : K (g) + FYMTNAU N : P : K (g) + FYMKAU N : P₂O₅ : K₂O (g) + FYM
1100 : 50 : 100 + 5 kg200 : 200 : 300 + 10 kg20 : 18 : 50 + 10 kg
2200 : 100 : 200 + 10 kg360 : 360 : 540 + 18 kg50 : 27 : 75 + 15 kg
3300 : 200 : 300 + 15 kg520 : 520 : 780 + 26 kg100 : 36 : 100 + 25 kg
4400 : 300 : 400 + 20 kg680 : 680 : 1020 + 34 kg100 : 36 : 100 + 25 kg
5500 : 400 : 500 + 25 kg840 : 840 : 1260 + 42 kg100 : 36 : 100 + 25 kg
6600 : 500 : 600 + 30 kg1000 : 1000 : 1500 + 50 kg250 : 172 : 200 + 40 kg
7700 : 500 : 700 + 35 kg1000 : 1000 : 1500 + 50 kg250 : 172 : 200 + 40 kg
8–9not listed1000 : 1000 : 1500 + 50 kg400 : 144 : 400 + 50 kg
101000 : 500 : 1000 + 50 kg1000 : 1000 : 1500 + 50 kg400 : 144 : 400 + 50 kg
11+1000 : 500 : 1000 + 50 kg1000 : 1000 : 1500 + 50 kg500 : 360 : 750 + 75 kg

NHB does not list years 8–9, so keep the year-7 dose until year 10. TNAU gives the year-1 dose and the dose from year 6; we raise it evenly in between. KAU gives its dose in age bands.

Converting nutrient grams into bags

Urea has 46% N, so 1 kg N = 2.17 kg urea. SSP has 16% P₂O₅, so 1 kg P₂O₅ = 6.25 kg SSP. DAP (18:46:0) gives 1 kg P₂O₅ in 2.17 kg and adds 0.39 kg N, so cut urea by that much. MOP has 60% K₂O, so 1 kg K₂O = 1.67 kg MOP. The calculator does this for you.

Which recommendation to follow

All three come from public bodies, but they were set for different conditions. The NHB schedule is the national reference. TNAU (Tamil Nadu) gives the highest doses, for well-irrigated orchards. KAU (Kerala) is lower and adds green leaves and wood ash. In Gujarat, follow Junagadh or Navsari Agricultural University or your KVK where they give a figure, and use NHB as the base. If you have a Soil Health Card, adjust the dose: a common rule in Indian packages is about 25% more for a nutrient the card shows as low and 25% less where it shows high.

When to apply

  • NHB: all manure and half the N, P and K at the start of the monsoon (June–July); the other half at the end of the monsoon (September–October).
  • KAU: young trees get the full dose once, in May–June. Bearing trees get two equal doses, in May–June and August–September.
  • TNAU: manure and fertilizer once, in September–October.

Whichever you follow, do not push nitrogen and water in the month before flowering. TNAU's drip schedule stops fertigation about 30 days before flowering; a well-fed tree that gets water then often puts out new leaves instead of flowers.

Where to put it

Feeder roots sit under the outer canopy, not at the trunk. TNAU says to spread fertilizer from about 45–90 cm from the trunk out to the edge of the canopy. For older trees NHB suggests a ring about 50 cm from the trunk mixed into the top 15 cm of soil, or trenches 25 cm wide and 25–30 cm deep about 2 m from the trunk. KAU uses trenches 30 cm deep, 2.5–3 m from the trunk on grown trees. Apply into moist soil and cover it.

Drip fertigation for high-density orchards

For high-density mango at 5 × 5 m (400 trees per hectare), TNAU recommends 1.0 kg N, 0.5 kg P and 1.0 kg K per bearing tree per year through drip, given every week and split by stage:

StageNPK
After harvest (2 months)25%50%25%
Pre-flowering (2 months)40%30%20%
Flowering to fruit set (2 months)20%20%25%
Fruit development (4 months)15%0%30%

TNAU notes that drip uses about a third of the water of basin irrigation. JAU has tested high-density Kesar at 3 × 2.5 m in South Saurashtra; the calculator has that spacing too.

Organic fertilizer for mango trees

All three recommendations already include organic manure: from 5–10 kg of FYM for a one-year tree up to 50–75 kg for a grown tree. KAU also suggests about 25 kg of green leaves and 10–15 kg of wood ash per grown tree. Manure alone rarely supplies the full nitrogen and potash dose at these rates, which is why all three pair it with fertilizer. Vermicompost and other organic sources can replace part of the FYM; check the nutrient content on the bag.

Micronutrients and Epsom salt

NHB advises micronutrients only where a shortage is seen, given as foliar sprays. Epsom salt is magnesium sulphate: it helps only if a leaf or soil test shows magnesium is short, so do not add it by default. Zinc and boron are the shortages most often reported in mango; confirm with a soil or leaf test and follow your university or KVK for the dose.

Which fertilizer helps fruit size

No fertilizer can promise bigger fruit; size depends on crop load, water and weather as much as on feeding. Potash is the nutrient most tied to fruit filling, which is why TNAU's drip schedule gives the largest share of potash (30%) during fruit development, with regular water in that period. Too much nitrogen late in the season tends to push leaves rather than fruit.

Questions farmers ask

Which is the best fertilizer for mango trees?

There is no single best product. Mango needs a balanced dose of nitrogen, phosphorus and potash that grows with the tree's age, plus farmyard manure. Urea, SSP or DAP, and MOP supply this. Add micronutrients only if a soil or leaf test shows a shortage.

How much NPK per mango tree?

NHB gives about 100 g N and 100 g K per year of the tree's age, with phosphorus rising from 50 g to 500 g, reaching 1 kg N, 500 g P and 1 kg K with 50 kg FYM from about year 10. TNAU's dose from year 6 is 1.0 kg N, 1.0 kg P and 1.5 kg K with 50 kg FYM.

Is Epsom salt good for mango trees?

Only when a leaf or soil test shows magnesium is short. Epsom salt is magnesium sulphate; it does not replace N, P and K and is not needed in a routine schedule.

Which fertilizer increases mango fruit size?

No fertilizer can guarantee bigger fruit. Potash during fruit development, with regular water, supports fruit filling; TNAU's drip schedule gives 30% of the year's potash in that stage.

When should I fertilize mango trees?

NHB: half at the start of the monsoon (June–July) and half at its end (September–October). KAU: May–June and August–September for bearing trees. Avoid nitrogen and water in the month before flowering.

How much urea, DAP and MOP for one mango tree?

For the NHB dose of a grown tree (1 kg N, 500 g P₂O₅, 1 kg K₂O): about 1.09 kg DAP, 1.75 kg urea and 1.67 kg MOP, or 3.1 kg SSP, 2.17 kg urea and 1.67 kg MOP. Use the calculator for other ages.
